findings.summary: Missing try/finally in CancelCodingAgentButton.cancel: if cancelCodingAgent rejects, setBusy(false) is never called and the button spinner runs forever
findings.failure_scenario: User clicks 'Cancel Coding Agent'. setBusy(true) fires, showing the spinner. The underlying cancelCodingAgent message-passing promise rejects (e.g., network fault, extension deactivation, timeout). The rejected promise unwinds without running setBusy(false). The button remains disabled with a spinning icon permanently until the webview is reloaded. The CheckoutButton.onClick in the same file (line 248) correctly wraps the async body in try/finally for exactly this reason.

findings.summary: onHideAction is recreated every render; removeEventListener in the else branch passes a fresh function reference that never matches the one added, leaking click+keydown listeners on document with every open/close cycle
findings.failure_scenario: User opens the dropdown (split-right click). Two listeners (click, keydown) are added to document via addEventListener wrapping the current render's onHideAction. User clicks outside to dismiss. The effect re-runs with expanded=false and calls removeEventListener with a newly-created function wrapping a newly-created onHideAction -- a different reference from the one that was added. The old listeners remain permanently. Repeat 50 open/close cycles: 100 leaked listeners fire on every document click/keydown (all no-ops, but waste memory and add per-event overhead). The effect also has no cleanup function returned, so listeners from the final expanded=true state survive component unmount.
